chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hammad, from Al-Halabi, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), that he was asked

about the fasting woman who cooks in a pot and tastes the broth while looking at it, so he said: 'There is no problem.' He said, 'And he was asked about the woman who has a child and she is fasting, so she chews the bread and feeds it to him, so he said: 'There is no problem,' and the bird, if it were hers.'

key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem / It is permissible

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a fasting woman to taste food while cooking or feed her child by chewing bread?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) establishes that tasting food to check its flavor does not break the fast, provided the taste is not swallowed, a ruling that alleviates domestic burdens for fasting women. This hadith is foundational in Shia fiqh for distinguishing between mere tasting and actual consumption, emphasizing ease in daily religious practice. The extension to feeding birds highlights the broader principle of permissible acts that involve minor ingestion or transfer of food without nullifying the fast.
